findings.claim: The regression test unconditionally invokes macOS-only `plutil`, so it fails on Linux hosts even though the installer renders both launchd and systemd artifacts.
findings.evidence: New test line adds `plutil -lint "$OUTPUT_ROOT/ai.prometheus.sovereign-sync.plist" >/dev/null`; file tree includes Linux systemd artifacts under `shared/systemd`, and no constraint or acceptance criterion limits this test to macOS.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the lint with `if command -v plutil >/dev/null; then ...; fi`, or use a portable XML parser available in the test environment.

findings.claim: `ordered_changes` are ignored whenever a `changes` key exists, so historical ledgers with an empty or non-array `changes` field and populated `ordered_changes` are not imported as required.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion requires importing historical `ordered_changes` ledgers; `legacy_phase` now uses `progress.get("changes").or_else(|| progress.get("ordered_changes"))`, which never consults `ordered_changes` if `changes` is present, and `progress_uncertain_rows` uses the same pattern at line 3911.
findings.suggested_fix: Fallback to `ordered_changes` when `changes` is absent, non-array, or empty/otherwise unusable for the legacy schema being migrated, and add a regression test covering a ledger containing both keys.
